newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disappointed at European aid cut to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disappointed at European aid cut to Turkey.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it was "very disappointed" that the European parliament had voted to freeze aid to Turkey because of Ankara's human rights record.
"We're very disappointed because we think the European Union should work on making relations with Turkey more productive and closer," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"That's what we've argued for a long time. Turkey is a European country," Burns told reporters.
The Strasbourg parliament voted in a first reading of the 1997 European Union budget on Thursday to block hundreds of millions of dollars of aid to help Ankara set up a customs union with the EU.
The parliament will take a second and final reading of the 1997 EU budget in December.
The State Department has criticised Turkey's human rights record, including abuses committed in its decade-long war against Kurdish separatist guerrillas.
